findings.statement: Renting NVIDIA H100 GPUs on the cloud has risen 45% compared with December, indicating rising compute cost pressures for AI developers.
limitations: Evidence comes only from X (social) platform.
All items are in English; Arabic coverage is minimal.

findings.statement: Social posts highlight strong positive sentiment toward NVIDIA‑powered liquid‑cooled H100 AI servers, describing them as “massive” and “extremely popular for AI.”
limitations: Both pieces of evidence are from X platform.
Only English language content is represented.

findings.statement: Reviews praise Supermicro’s universal GPU systems that can house up to eight NVIDIA A100 or H100 GPUs with NVLink/NVSwitch, indicating favorable adoption among providers seeking high‑density AI compute.
limitations: Evidence limited to X platform and English language.

findings.statement: Ongoing AI chip shortages keep NVIDIA H100 prices high, and older H100 rentals now cost more than when new, creating cost‑related pain points for cloud providers.
limitations: All evidence originates from X platform and is in English.

findings.statement: Some commentators express negative sentiment toward NVIDIA’s market dominance, labeling CEO Jensen Huang as a national‑security risk, reflecting reputational concerns for partners.
limitations: Single piece of evidence from X platform; English only.

Older AI chips are still selling in a tight market.
